title: audit current FR_REGIONS
headline: FR_REGIONS (normalize.py:243-249) holds 14 entries over 4 canonical values (hdf, idf, naq, pdl). Scoping is exhaustively correct (sum(country_rows.values())==rows in all 6 profile files) and there is zero overlap with US_STATES/IN_STATES/ADDR_CANON. Two defects: the known missing self-map at line 252 (CONFIRMED code, ZERO measurable effect, independently re-confirmed) and a NEW order-dependence defect - line 334 does 'state = smap[ck]' with no break, so a later matched component OVERWRITES an earlier one: 'Paris, Hauts-de-France' -> hdf but 'Hauts-de-France, Paris' -> idf. The 9 departement keys are load-bearing (0.3266 dept-tok/row on test_s2), so thinning FR_REGIONS to 18 regions would be a large regression.
new_defect: normalize.py:334 assigns state=smap[ck] with no break, making state last-match-wins. Two comma-orderings of the same French address resolve to different regions. CONFIRMED by executing the real module. Blast radius bounded at <=388/952/923 France rows (0.150%/0.135%/0.126%).
second_new_defect: FR_REGIONS conflates 3 administrative levels in one flat namespace: 4 regions + 9 departements + 1 city (paris). 10/14 entries (71.4%) are not regions. CONFIRMED structural.

load_bearing_finding.claim: s1 is region-stated; s2/s3 are departement-stated. The 9 departement keys are load-bearing, not decoration.
load_bearing_finding.caveat_pas: 'pas' is also the ordinary French word 'step', so pas-de-calais is a loose upper bound; calais=55273 in s2 vs pas=14325, so most calais occurrences are the CITY not the departement
load_bearing_finding.caveat_loire: 'loire' unusable for loire atlantique because it also occurs in pays de la loire; used 'atlantique' instead (s2 loire=126216 vs atlantique=63697)
load_bearing_finding.implication: Deleting the departement keys would be a LARGE REGRESSION on 2 of 3 test sources. This is the highest-value warning for the follow-up tasks.

per_key_activity.probe_token_note: single-word keys use the key itself; multi-word keys use a distinctive sub-token (atlantique for loire atlantique, pas for pas de calais)

unmapped_regions.grand_est_caveat: grand=704 vs est=76 in s1 is 9:1; a co-occurring two-word region field would give ~1:1, so 'grand' is more likely street vocabulary (Grand Rue, Grande Place). Excluded from headline claims.
unmapped_regions.paca_caveat: provence=56 and cote=23 in s1 are at/below the truncation floor of 23, so presence is not established in s1; s2/s3 provence=119/116 vs cote=157/169 does not establish co-occurrence either.

gaps: No state-resolution field exists in the profile. by_country collects rows, name_empty, addr_empty, name_chars, addr_chars, name_tokens, num_digits, has_digit_name, has_comma, prefix_bad, dig5, dig6, alpha_only_addr, len_hist (build_profile.py:85-91). The '100.00%' resolution figure CANNOT be re-derived from the profile at all; corroborated only indirectly.

The profile records tokens, not components (ADDR_SPLIT.split then TOKEN_RE.findall, build_profile.py:126-127). No co-occurrence, no multi-word row counts, no separation of the city 'calais' from the key 'pas de calais'. Every 'affected rows' figure in this report is a labelled token-count UPPER bound.
The already_checked contradiction above is unresolved and unresolvable from the profile.

No French ground truth: all three train files have zero France rows, so no label can confirm which of hdf/idf/naq/pdl is correct. The claim that 'paris -> idf' is semantically right is SPECULATIVE; only its behavioural destructiveness is claimed.
Single-run figures. No variance estimate possible; no second pass over the raw TSVs (prohibited by the 1 GB RAM constraint).

recommendations_priority_ordered.action: Do NOT delete the departement keys. s2/s3 are departement-stated at 0.3266/0.3175 tok/row, i.e. up to 32.66%/31.75% of France rows. Expected effect of thinning to 18 regions: LARGE REGRESSION on 2 of 3 test sources.

Add a precedence rule at normalize.py:334 so a matched component cannot overwrite an earlier match. Cheapest fix and the only one that fixes WRONG answers rather than missing ones. Measure before/after; bounded at <=388/952/923 France rows.
Add a component-level field to build_profile.py (comma-split components, or at minimum a per-country count of rows whose address contains 2+ state-map keys). Without it F4/F8/F12 stay unresolvable.

Move 'paris' out of the state map into a city list, so a city is never consumed at line 335 and never competes with a region for state. Behaviour change on ~0.13-0.15% of France rows; measure, do not assume.
Rename or re-document the dictionary as a mixed-level region+departement+city gazetteer. Cost: a comment. No behavioural change.

Add the CONFIRMED unmapped regions: bretagne, lorraine, alsace, normandie, auvergne, bourgogne, champagne, picardie. grand est is LIKELY at most, PACA is SPECULATIVE; both need the component-level field first.
Add the self-map loop entry (US_STATES, IN_STATES, FR_REGIONS). Expected effect: EXACTLY ZERO on this dataset. Symmetry only; do not claim a score change.
Leave 'aisne' and 'vendee' alone. They cost nothing measurable; they are the only forward-looking coverage for HDF/PDL.
Do not use 'ile' or 'le' counts as evidence about Ile-de-France, and do not cite the exact partition without citing the F12 contradiction.

ADDR_CANON_FR:211 maps single-letter tokens b->bis, t->ter, r->rue, q/qu->quai, all/al->allee. Verified: '9 Rue T, HDF' yields toks ['9','rue','ter','hdf']. Plausible token-noise source, but it does NOT interact with FR_REGIONS (no FR_REGIONS key is a single letter). Flagged to the ADDR_CANON_FR owner, not claimed as a FR_REGIONS defect.
